findings.detail: why_wrong says だけ goes with a positive verb, not with ありません. だけ can take a negative (Xだけ たべません = X is the one thing I don't eat); here it just gives the wrong meaning.
findings.fix: だけ: "みっかだけ ありません means 'only three days are missing', not 'only three days'; with ありません use しか."

findings.detail: すきじゃないです and すきではないです are common, correct polite negatives of すきです and are not accepted.
findings.fix: accepted: ["すきでは ありません", "すきじゃないです", "すきではないです", "すきじゃありません", "すきではありません"]

findings.detail: 'Setting a task aside to deal with later' is not a meaning of ておきます; ておく marks doing the action (now or later) so it is done/handled, or leaving a state as is.
findings.fix: explain: "ておきます can also mean leaving something as it is, or getting a task done so it is taken care of. Ask someone to leave things as they are with ておいて ください."

findings.detail: でんわすると いいました ('she said') is also correct for the English line and would be marked wrong.
findings.fix: accepted: ["いっていました", "いいました"]

use_tag_disagreements.why: This point is leaving things as they are, mostly as ておいて ください requests; it is not about stating a plan.
〜という いみです explains what a word or sign means; it is not passing on something heard or read. No existing use fits well; consider a new 'explaining meaning' use.
